df4c0e58a1.q: What is Uber for Business and how does it differ from consumer Uber?
df4c0e58a1.a: Uber for Business is the enterprise layer that sits on top of the consumer app. It helps organizations manage and optimize their mobility and meal spend, allowing employees to use Uber on a centralized platform instead of personal accounts while giving organizations visibility and controls over employee spending.

3b08b5342c.q: How has Uber for Business structured its sales enablement team to balance global consistency with regional market needs?
3b08b5342c.a: Uber for Business implemented a central enablement and regional enablement structure. Regional enablement leads sit in-market with sellers to respond to market-specific needs, while central enablement focuses on scalable programs like playbooks that work globally. Regional teams have autonomy but communicate weekly with central teams to share best practices and identify scalable solutions.

4f4c1b709c.q: What are the key metrics Uber for Business uses to measure success of new AI tool implementations?
4f4c1b709c.a: Adoption is the biggest success metric—how sellers are adopting and utilizing new tools. Performance metrics are also tracked, including uptick in conversion rates or ramp time, anything that indicates the tool is helping move the needle for the business.

1d6c260f91.q: How does Uber for Business onboard new account executives to hit the ground running on day one?
1d6c260f91.a: Onboarding is structured as a mix of on-demand learning and a week-long virtual live boot camp via Zoom, followed by manager coaching and completion activities. BDRs begin prospecting and warming up leads before the new AE's start date so they have qualified leads ready on their first day to accelerate time to first opportunity.
